examples.ko: 새로 등산화 한 켤레 사야 해요.
examples.en: I need to buy a new pair of hiking boots.
Tie your hiking boot laces tightly.
These hiking boots are light and don't slip.
I'll change into my hiking boots and set out.

explain: 산에 오를 때 신는 튼튼한 신발이에요. 신발은 '켤레'로 세고 '신다, 벗다'와 함께 써요. 가볍게 걸을 때 신는 '운동화'와는 구별해서 말해요.

phrases.en: I put on hiking boots and climbed the mountain.
phrases.nuance_en: Shoes go with 신다, and you can connect it as 신고.

phrases.en: I came home and took off my hiking boots.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 벗다 to take shoes off.

phrases.en: They are new hiking boots, so my feet hurt a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새'를 앞에 붙이면 새로 산 신발이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 새 in front means newly bought boots.

explain_en: These are sturdy shoes worn when climbing mountains. Shoes are counted with '켤레' and used with '신다' (put on) and '벗다' (take off). People distinguish them from '운동화' (sneakers) used for casual walking.

examples.en: This weekend I'm going on a spring outing with my family.

examples.ko: 벚꽃이 피어서 봄나들이 나온 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The cherry blossoms are out, so many people are on spring outings.
The weather today is perfect for a spring outing.
Where should we go for our spring outing this year?
During spring outing season the highways get very congested.
I set out with the kids on a spring outing to the park.

explain: '나들이'는 가까운 곳에 놀러 다녀오는 것이라서 '봄나들이를 가다/나가다/떠나다'로 써요. 학교나 단체에서 가는 '소풍'보다 가족, 친구와 가볍게 나가는 느낌이에요. '꽃구경'과 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This weekend I'm going on a spring outing with my family.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic verb pairing.
phrases.en_equiv: to go on a spring outing

phrases.en: I set off to the sea with friends for a spring outing.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a feel of heading somewhat farther away.
phrases.en_equiv: to set off on a spring outing

phrases.en: In spring I want to go see the flowers.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical activity on a spring outing.

explain_en: '나들이' is a short trip somewhere nearby, so you say '봄나들이를 가다/나가다/떠나다'. It feels more like a casual trip with family or friends than a school or group '소풍'. It often appears alongside '꽃구경'.

examples.en: I saw a big shark for the first time at the aquarium.
The big shark swims slowly in the water.
Children get scared when they hear shark stories.

examples.ko: 바다에는 사람을 공격하지 않는 상어도 많아요.
examples.en: There are also many sharks in the sea that don't attack people.

examples.ko: 동생은 상어 모양 인형을 안고 자요.
examples.en: My younger sibling sleeps hugging a shark-shaped doll.
The news said a shark appeared near the beach.

explain: 한국에서는 동요 '아기 상어'가 아주 유명해서 아이들도 잘 아는 단어예요. 동물은 '마리'로 세어서 '상어 한 마리'라고 해요. '고래상어', '백상어'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 종류를 나눠요.

phrases.en: I saw one shark in the sea.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with the counter '마리'.

phrases.en: The kids love the Baby Shark song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 동요 이름이라 아이들과 이야기할 때 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a well-known children's song, common when talking with kids.

phrases.en: The great white shark is very fast and scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상어' 앞에 말을 붙여 종류를 나눈 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name made by adding a word before '상어' to name a type.

explain_en: The children's song 아기 상어 (Baby Shark) is hugely popular in Korea, so even kids know this word. Animals are counted with 마리: 상어 한 마리. Kinds are named by adding a word in front, as in 고래상어 (whale shark) and 백상어 (great white shark).

examples.ko: 겨울에는 집 근처 스케이트장이 문을 열어요.
examples.en: In winter, the skating rink near my house opens.
I met my friends at the skating rink on the weekend.
How much is admission to the skating rink in front of City Hall?
The kids have fun at the rink even while falling down.
It takes about thirty minutes by subway to get to the skating rink.
There are too many people at the skating rink today.

explain: '스케이트를 타다'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 얼음 위에서 타는 곳이라서 '아이스링크'라고도 하고, 스포츠 경기용으로는 '빙상장'이라는 말도 써요. 가는 곳이니까 '스케이트장에 가다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: On Sunday I go to the skating rink with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소로 이동할 때 '에 가다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'e gada' when going to the place.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the skating rink

phrases.en: In winter I skate at the ice rink.
phrases.nuance_en: Another word with the same meaning as 'seukeiteujang'.

phrases.en: Skating at the rink is fun.
phrases.nuance_en: A good phrase to memorize as a pair with 'seukeiteu-reul tada'.

explain_en: Learn it together with '스케이트를 타다' (to skate). People also say '아이스링크', and '빙상장' is used for sports venues. Since it is a place you go to, say '스케이트장에 가다'.

examples.ko: 올봄에는 벚꽃 구경을 꼭 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: This spring I definitely want to go see the cherry blossoms.
The fine dust this spring wasn't as bad as last year.
This spring I finally found a new job.
I've been jogging every morning since this spring.

examples.ko: 올봄은 비가 자주 와서 꽃이 일찍 졌어요.
examples.en: It rained often this spring, so the flowers fell early.

examples.ko: 올봄 졸업 사진을 찍으러 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to school to take graduation photos this spring.

explain: '올여름', '올가을', '올겨울'처럼 한 단어로 붙여 써요. 지난해 봄은 '지난봄', 다음 해 봄은 '내년 봄'이라고 해요. '올봄에는'처럼 계획이나 바람을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to travel this spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올봄'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used widely with almost the same meaning as 'olbom'.

phrases.en: I moved last spring.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the spring of last year.

phrases.en: This spring I'm going to start exercising.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'eneun' it emphasizes a plan or wish.

explain_en: It is written as one word, like '올여름', '올가을' and '올겨울'. Last year's spring is '지난봄' and next year's is '내년 봄'. It often appears as '올봄에는' when talking about plans or hopes.

examples.en: There is a big persimmon tree in the landlord's yard.

explain: '집주인'은 집을 가진 사람이고 '주인집'은 그 주인이 사는 집이나 그 가족을 가리키는 느낌이에요. 세 들어 사는 사람이 이야기할 때 자주 써요. 옛날 이야기에서는 일하러 간 집, 즉 주인이 사는 집을 뜻하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The landlord's wife gave me some kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세 들어 사는 사람이 집주인 가족을 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by a tenant for a woman in the landlord's family.

phrases.en: I live on the second floor of the landlord's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주인이 사는 집 안에서 세 들어 사는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when renting a part of the house where the owner lives.

phrases.en: The landlord's family is very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집주인과 그 가족을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the landlord together with their family.

explain_en: '집주인' is the person who owns the house, while '주인집' feels like the owner's home or the owner's family. Tenants often use it when talking. In old stories it can mean the house where one works, where the master lives.

t90.ax: The landlord fixed my broken lock.

examples.en: At the hospital, the doctor treats patients.
My tooth hurts, so I'm going to the dentist for treatment.

examples.ko: 이 병은 약으로 치료할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This illness can be treated with medicine.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 다친 다리를 잘 치료했어요.
examples.en: That doctor treated the injured leg well.

examples.ko: 일찍 치료하면 훨씬 빨리 나을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get treated early, you can recover much faster.

explain: 의사가 주어이면 '치료하다', 환자가 주어이면 '치료를 받다'를 써요. 병이 저절로 '낫다'와도 달라요. 기계나 물건은 '고치다'를 쓰고 '치료하다'는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I got treatment at the dentist.
phrases.nuance_en: When the patient is the subject, say 치료를 받다.

phrases.en: This medicine treats colds.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병/감기를 치료하다'처럼 낫게 하는 대상을 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair it with the illness being treated, such as 병 or 감기.

phrases.en: I am getting my tooth treated now.
phrases.nuance_en: Means treatment is in progress right now.

explain_en: With a doctor as subject it's '치료하다'; with the patient as subject it's '치료를 받다' (receive treatment). It differs from '낫다', which is getting better on its own. Machines and objects are '고치다', never '치료하다'.

dis.h: give medical care to cure an illness
gh: heal, especially wounds of the heart
a doctor sees and treats patients
give quick first-aid care on the spot

p.n: 진료하다 means seeing and examining the patient.

t90.ax: That doctor treated the injured leg well.

examples.en: My paternal grandfather takes a walk every morning.
My grandfather on my father's side told me old stories.
On New Year's Day I bowed to my paternal grandfather.
My paternal grandfather's house is in the countryside.
I take after my paternal grandfather, so I'm tall.

explain: 아버지의 아버지를 말하고, 어머니의 아버지는 '외할아버지'예요. 직접 부를 때는 그냥 '할아버지'라고 해요. '친할아버지께서', '친할아버지께'처럼 높임 표현과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: My paternal grandfather is reading the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어를 높일 때 '께서'를 붙이고 동사에도 '-으시-'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '께서' for the subject and '-으시-' on the verb to show respect.

phrases.en: On holidays we gather at my paternal grandfather's house.
phrases.nuance_en: '댁' is the honorific for 'house' when speaking of a grandfather's home.

phrases.en: I called my paternal grandfather.
phrases.nuance_en: '께' and '드리다' show respect toward the grandfather.

explain_en: It means your father's father, while your mother's father is '외할아버지'. When addressing him directly you just say '할아버지'. It is used with honorific forms like '친할아버지께서' and '친할아버지께'.

examples.en: We pitched a tent by the clear river.
We ate ramen with my family inside the tent.
It rained, so the tent got completely wet.

examples.ko: 이 텐트는 가벼워서 혼자 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: This tent is light, so I can carry it alone.
Can I rent a tent at the campsite?
At night it's very cold outside the tent.

explain: '텐트를 치다'가 자연스러운 짝이에요. '세우다'도 틀리진 않지만 '치다'를 더 많이 써요. 접을 때는 '텐트를 걷다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: We pitched a tent at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 텐트를 세울 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural verb for setting up a tent.

phrases.en: I got up in the morning and took down the tent.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take down and pack away the tent.

phrases.example: 저는 텐트에서 자 본 적이 없어요.
phrases.en: I have never slept in a tent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 캠핑할 때 텐트 안에서 잠을 잔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means sleeping inside a tent, for example when camping.

explain_en: The natural pairing is 텐트를 치다 (pitch a tent); 세우다 works but 치다 is more common. To take it down, say 텐트를 걷다.
